decisions.reason: The existing message-539 MODIFY already limits valid referral codes to NFTs minted by the new active contract and invalidates old-contract mint numbers.
The existing FAQ says every NFT mint number is a permanent referral code, which must be qualified after the client accepted restarting at #1 and excluding old-contract NFTs from project systems.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hmmmmm... well, I do think that'd be best. 
I'm not too worried about the lost copies in the old contract

value_updates.referral_operation: Each NFT minted by the new active contract uses its mint number, restarting at NFT #1, as its permanent referral code; old-contract NFT mint numbers are excluded from project systems. Coded referrals earn $5 and current prize tickets, while a mint without a referral code sends the commission and tickets to a random existing eligible NFT holder.

decisions.reason: The existing message-539 MODIFY already requires dashboard systems to use new-contract NFTs and exclude old-contract copies.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already scopes public referral aggregates to new-contract activity and excludes old-contract referral data.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already limits random reward recipients to eligible holders in the new active contract.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already excludes old-contract reward and ticket data from dashboard accounting.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already restarts displayed mint statistics at NFT #1 for the new active contract and excludes old-contract copies.
Confirmation emails remain required to contain the mint number generated by the completed mint; switching the active contract does not change the email contents or delivery behavior.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already restarts ticket draws under the new active contract and excludes old-contract NFTs from the active ticket system.
The existing message-539 MODIFY already restricts eligible tickets and winners to the new active contract and prevents carryover of old-contract draw state.
The accepted contract switch does not alter the requirement that active NFTs expose their mint-number referral code in metadata, and the old contract and its existing metadata remain in existence.

The prescribed messages remain valid: a randomly selected holder from the new active contract is still an existing NFT holder, while contract-specific eligibility is governed by the validation requirement.
